members.name: Terry McCullum
members.bio: Terry McCullum, MSW, MA, MDiv, was CEO of a large charitable non-profit organization (LOFT Community Services, www.loftcs.org) for 35 years. During that time he was part of the development of many new programs serving homeless young people and adults with serious mental health challenges by providing a wide range of flexible community supports and supportive housing plus supporting seniors with disabilities coming out of hospital with no safe place to live. Each year it serves over 7000 individuals with a mission to “provide unwavering support and hope”. Terry has a strong passion for the charitable sector and has seen firsthand the ability of charitable donations to spur innovation, risk taking, new program creation and expansion of services to those in need in our communities.

members.name: Warren MacKenzie
members.bio: Warren MacKenzie as the Head of Financial Planning at Optimize Wealth Management is responsible for delivering advice rooted in sound investment principles to help clients achieve their financial goals. Over his 30-year career within the financial industry, Warren has become well know as an advocate for investor education and is the author of The Unbiased Advisor, Zen and The Art of Wealth, and co-author of New Rules of Retirement and The C.A.R.P. Financial Planning Guide. For The Life Institute Warren teaches a course called “Joy of Money –How much is Enough”. He is a regular contributor to the ‘Financial Facelift’ column in The Globe and Mail. Warren is a Chartered Professional Accountant and also holds the Certified Investment Management Analyst Designation (CIMA) and the Chartered Investment Manager Designation (CIM). Warren works primarily with clients who are in retirement or close to retirement, and he focuses on calculating their “Essential Capital” and “Surplus Capital”. He knows that when clients have confidence in their “Surplus Capital” number they get to enjoy their retirement even more. Retirees have only a few ways to dispose their surplus capital before they die. They can use it to maintain a more expensive lifestyle, they can give to their heirs sooner rather than later, they can give it to charity, or they can give it to the government in the form of tax. When clients understand what is essential and what is surplus –they’re free to choose the best way to enjoy their capital.

members.name: Linda Reed
members.bio: Linda Reed, MA, MBA, Certif. Prof. Coach, began her career in her home town of Vancouver. Her first major job was as a Regional Administrator in the Real Estate Division of Royal Trust. Creating and managing budgets for 19 sales offices in the Pacific Region, overseeing millions of dollars in trust funds and authorizing all payables gave her a good start in the business world. When the division was merged with the Alberta region, she moved to Toronto to further her career. Breaking into the Toronto market in a recession with no contacts took a year, but opportunities opened up. She started up and managed the Toronto location of the New York-based Learning Annex, an adult education company. She added regional director responsibilities and oversaw offices in Atlanta, Boston and Washington, DC. She moved on to join Insight Educational Services, a conference company serving the legal and senior executive markets. She left to start up her own executive conference business and ran it out of her home for 20 years. The conferences were offered in numerous cities throughout Canada and some U.S. locations. She also travelled internationally to locate sites and produce weeklong executive development programs. Then she changed course, sold her company and took a coaching certification as a Life Coach, specializing in transition coaching, which includes retirement. She developed and delivered a retirement workshop, coached clients on the phone, and set up a charitable Foundation to give back to her community and the world.

members.name: Michael Alexander
members.bio: Over 20 years ago, Michael Alexander became one of North America’s leading experts on the subject of inheritance after publishing his best-selling book, How to Inherit Money: A Guide to Making Good Financial Decisions After Losing Someone You Love (HarperCollins, 1997). Alerting the public to the inheritance revolution – the $11 trillion dollar inheritance windfall North American baby boomers were about to receive – Michael warned that the experience of inheritance can give rise to internal tensions and contradictions that can impair personal insight and sound financial judgment. Due to the success of How to Inherit, Michael became a sought-after professional speaker and media commentator on legal and financial issues. In 2005, Michael appeared as a self-represented litigant at the Supreme Court of Canada, where he obtained a unanimous judgment against State Farm U.S., which had the effect of preventing insurance companies from forcing homeowners across the country to pay out hundreds of millions of dollars in new insurance premiums. Later that same year, he published his second book, Competing Against America (Wiley and Sons), which explored the legal, political and social causes of Canada’s declining productivity and innovation. Michael holds law degrees from the University of Toronto and Columbia University, where he also studied political science and philosophy at the graduate level. While holding the Laidlaw Fellowship in Law and Political Science, he also studied at the Committee on Social Thought at the University of Chicago.

members.name: Andrew Jenkins
members.bio: Andrew Jenkins earned a BA in Economics from Laurentian University, a BFA in Film Production from York University, and an MBA from the Rotman School of Management at the University of Toronto. Based in Toronto, Canada, he was formerly the Head of Social Media Strategy for Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and has worked with a diverse list of companies in North America and Europe, including CIBC, BMO Nesbitt Burns, Rogers, Bell Canada, Sirius XM, The Globe and Mail, World Vision Canada, InfoSpace and The Aga Khan Foundation. A regular international speaker and panellist at numerous industry conferences and events, he also teaches a course on Social Media Strategies for the Enterprise at the University of Toronto’s School of Continuing Studies. Andrew is Principal of Volterra, a professional services firm specializing in social media and social selling strategies. He has just recently authored and released his new book Social Media Marketing for Business: Scaling an Integrated Social Media Strategy Across Your Organization.
